title: App-held pane pool: a 4-running cap and a queue, through one action
notes:
Design source: /tmp/pane-pool-review.md (research card 26f1e38e; copy the parts you use into the docs, /tmp does not last). User decisions: a paused worker and a blocked worker both hold their slot; one cap for the whole app; queue first-in first-out, main can reorder and withdraw.

The user's bar: a clear, engineered design that goes through actions properly, not code scattered wherever it fits. Concretely:
- Decisions in one module, src/main/workers/pane-pool.ts with its test (workflow-rule-2): holdsSlot(look), nextToStart(entries, running, cap, gate) answering the entry or the reason the queue is held, the budget gate where no limit configured never holds.
- One action owns every change to the pool (actions-rule-1): src/main/actions/pane/queue.ts with pane.start, pane.queue, pane.unqueue, beside claim/dispatch/release, each with a test. Every door that starts new work (pane start, board ship, the review sweep, the MCP tools) calls pane.start; none counts slots or reads the queue itself. Restore, pane send and New Claude never queue. Add no new bypass to bypasses.test.ts.
- Draining is one function the action exposes, called from the state changes that free a slot (worker done, release, finish, agent exit) in session-requests.ts: wiring only, no decision there. Nothing new in main.ts beyond passing ports (it is over the size limit).
- The pane and worktree are chosen when an entry starts, never when queued.
- Persisted in pane-queue.json through one store module; setting workers.cap (default 4) read through the settings action.
- Answers: 'starting <pane>' or 'queued <id>, <position>'; main gets a notice when a queued entry starts. Holding a card until another card merges: --after <card>.
- Docs: a workers decision for the slot rule and the pool, ship and settings READMEs, and the main session's instructions edited to drop slot counting, claim-then-run and the budget-before-each-round paragraph.
First PR is the pool, action, store, setting and doors. The workers-popup view of the queue (with a withdraw key, help.ts, settings row) is a second card once this merges.
